name: Bijie Landslide Dataset: Satellite Optical Imagery and Digital Elevation Models
description: The Bijie Landslide Dataset is a specialized remote sensing geohazard detection and segmentation benchmark curated by the Photogrammetry and Computer Vision (GPCV) Lab at Wuhan University and the State Key Laboratory of Geohazard Prevention at Chengdu University of Technology. Covering mountainous terrain in Bijie City, Guizhou Province, China, the dataset integrates TripleSat optical satellite imagery (0.8-meter ground resolution) and corresponding Digital Elevation Models (DEM, 2-meter resolution). It comprises 2,773 image samples, consisting of 770 landslide-positive samples and 2,003 non-landslide background samples. For all 770 landslide occurrences, the dataset provides optical image patches, DEM elevation rasters, binary segmentation mask images, and precise boundary coordinate polygons. The sample count reflects verified image-DEM sample units rather than isolated polygon vertices.

citation.paper_title: Landslide detection from an open satellite imagery and digital elevation model dataset using attention boosted convolutional neural networks

provenance.collection_method: Extracted from TripleSat optical satellite constellation (0.8m) captured between May and August 2018 paired with an airborne/satellite Digital Elevation Model (2m) in Bijie City, Guizhou Province.
provenance.curation_notes: Annotated by geological remote sensing experts. Contains 770 verified landslide occurrences with pixel masks and polygon coordinates, and 2,003 negative background samples.
